test_description: Compile the same playbook twice in a temp dir, diff manifest.json (ignoring generated_at), assert identical — proving compile output depends solely on source, not wall-clock time
test_assertions: Two compiles of identical source produce identical manifest content (ignoring generated_at)
Two compiles of identical source produce identical runstate content (ignoring generated_at)
A --deterministic flag or config option suppresses timestamps entirely
change_description: Either omit generated_at from the hash-sensitive portion of the manifest, or add a --deterministic flag that uses a stable value (e.g. git HEAD hash) instead of wall-clock time
why_this_correction: Evidence from observe phase: commands-compile.ts:188 embeds generated_at: new Date().toISOString() in manifest metadata, and line 252 does the same in runstate metadata. This means every compile produces different output even with identical source, breaking DAG discovery determinism — the idempotency test (compile twice, diff manifests) always fails. Fixing this prevents an entire class of 'same source, different output' bugs and directly encodes the Fingerprint Determinism model rule into the compile pipeline.
